s1.syndrome_frame: Systemic infection with multi-organ involvement in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Acute hypoxic respiratory failure and septic shock
Elevated CSF opening pressure and high red-cell count
key_facts: Patient has known HIV/AIDS with CD4 count <20 cells/µL
Patient has prior intravenous drug use and active tobacco dependence
Patient reported one month of poor appetite and weight loss
Patient had several days of diarrhea without abdominal pain, vomiting, cough, or dyspnea
Patient was febrile (39.4 °C) and hypotensive (91/60 mmHg) on examination
Patient had leukocytosis (31 151/µL) and hyponatremia (Na 121 mEq/L) on initial labs
Chest radiograph was clear initially
Abdominal ultrasound revealed hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, and enlarged peripancreatic lymph nodes
Patient developed acute hypoxic respiratory failure and septic shock requiring intubation
Lumbar puncture demonstrated an opening pressure of 35 cm H₂O, 1825 RBCs/dL, 1 WBC/dL, glucose 65 mg/dL, and protein 36 mg/dL

shortlist.label: Disseminated tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has known HIV/AIDS with CD4 count <20 cells/µL and symptoms consistent with systemic infection

shortlist.label: Disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has advanced HIV and systemic illness, making MAC a likely opportunistic infection

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has HIV/AIDS and symptoms of respiratory failure, which is consistent with PCP

shortlist.label: Cryptococcal meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has HIV/AIDS and symptoms of meningitis, which is consistent with cryptococcal infection

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has HIV/AIDS and symptoms of systemic infection, which is consistent with CMV

raw.rationale: The patient's advanced HIV with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL, systemic illness, and absence of clear evidence pointing to other infections make Disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex a likely diagnosis, especially given the patient's fever, weight loss, and hepatosplenomegaly

rejected.label: Disseminated tuberculosis
rejected.why: Although possible, the initial sputum smears for acid-fast bacilli were negative, and there's no clear indication of tuberculosis over Mycobacterium avium complex in the provided information

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: Bronchoalveolar lavage was negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii cultures, making this less likely

rejected.label: Cryptococcal meningitis
rejected.why: While the lumbar puncture showed an elevated opening pressure, the presence of 1825 RBCs/dL and the clinical context do not strongly support this diagnosis without further evidence of Cryptococcus

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
rejected.why: There's no specific evidence provided that directly points to a cytomegalovirus infection as the primary cause of the patient's condition
